title: Marcos: ASEAN Summit a time to address current challenges of the region
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Sunday said the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits is a time for member states to address the challenges faced by the region, as the three-day international…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Sunday said the 49th Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits is a time for member states to address the challenges faced by the region, as the three-day international conference officially began.
These challenges include transnational crimes involving trafficking, cybercrime, and online scams. There is also a need to strengthen maritime cooperation.

"Over the coming days, alongside our external partners, the choices we will make shape how ASEAN meets the challenges of today, seizes the opportunities of tomorrow, and prepares the region for the coming generations," Marcos said during his opening speech.
The Philippines chairs the 2026 ASEAN with the theme "Navigating Our Future, Together."

"As the Balangay reminds us, no journey is made by following one direction alone. It requires trust among those who travel together, the strength to adjust to changing conditions, and a shared sense of commitment towards our shared goals and common destinations," the President said, as he described the ASEAN 2026 logo.
During the opening ceremony, the new ASEAN emblem was unveiled.
Marcos and ASEAN secretary-general Dr Kao Kin Hourn also led the updated presentation of the updated flag and certificate.
Hla Hla Aung of Myanmar was awarded this year's ASEAN Prize.

A researcher and regional advocate in disaster management and preparedness, Aung was recognized for her commitment to advancing disaster resilience, particularly in turning scientific research to policy advocacy and community empowerment.
Marcos and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos earlier welcomed each delegate upon arrival at the PICC. —KG, GMA News
